inputs.text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, the killing in Gaza is still going on—airstrikes, drones, gunfire, shelling, and fire directed at fishermen. The “ceasefire” sounds like a label designed to reassure the public and shield powerful institutions from scrutiny while the violence continues. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the drones “never stop buzzing overhead.” That’s the reality the official story wants pushed into the background, because silence makes ongoing destruction easier to tolerate.
